title: Effective atom-dimer bands of three-body lattice systems at strong coupling: exact critical mass ratios and a statistics-quasimomentum duality
abstract: We study three particles on the square lattice with contact interactions of infinite strength, for all total quasimomenta, for three statistics: three identical bosons, two identical fermions plus a third particle, and two identical bosons plus a third particle. Previous work treated only the trimer and zero quasimomentum. Here the atom-dimer sector is analyzed on the whole Brillouin zone. A Feshbach-Schur reduction onto the infinitely degenerate eigenvalue 1 of the pair-contact operator gives explicit effective Hamiltonians with proved first-order error. The threshold problem reduces to a 4x4 Hermitian matrix criterion built from the two-point resistances of the square lattice, and hence to a quartic polynomial. This yields the complete atom-dimer zone and the critical mass ratio on the Brillouin zone, with bound between 1 and pi/(pi-2), and closed forms at all symmetry points. We prove: the zones in closed form; the critical mass ratio with exact value pi/(pi-2) at zero quasimomentum, reproducing a numerical value; at most two atom-dimer states for every quasimomentum and mass ratio; the onset laws, an essential singularity on the zone boundary and a linear-over-logarithm onset in the pure p-wave; two exact dualities showing that a change of statistics is equivalent to a shift of quasimomentum by pi; and the global range of the second fermionic threshold. The onset laws admit a renormalization-group reading: the inverse lattice Green function is a marginal s-wave coupling, binding energies arise by dimensional transmutation with lattice scale 16, and the zone boundary is of marginal (BCS/Kondo) type rather than of Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless type. All constants are verified independently by lattice quadrature, computer algebra, exact diagonalisation, and infinite-lattice solvers.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates the effective energy bands for three-body quantum systems on a lattice under strong contact interactions. By employing Feshbach-Schur reduction, the authors derive explicit Hamiltonians and determine the critical mass ratios governing the existence of bound states across the entire Brillouin zone. The results establish exact mathematical dualities between particle statistics and momentum shifts.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the effective energy bands for three-body systems (bosonic and fermionic) interacting via contact potentials on a lattice in the strong coupling limit.
main_result: It derives explicit effective Hamiltonians and determines the complete atom-dimer zone and the critical mass ratio $\pi/(\pi-2)$ at zero quasimomentum, establishing exact dualities between statistics and quasimomentum shifts.
method: The methodology involves Feshbach-Schur reduction onto the degenerate eigenvalue subspace, followed by solving a threshold problem formulated as a $4 	imes 4$ Hermitian matrix criterion.
model_or_system: The system consists of three particles (bosons or fermions) on a square lattice ($\mathbb{Z}^2$) with contact interactions of infinite strength ($\mu 	o \infty$). The analysis focuses on the 'atom-dimer sector' of the three-body Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Effective Hamiltonians ($h_B, h_F$), critical mass ratio $\gamma_c(\mathbf{K})$, and the onset laws for bound states.
important_parameters: Strong coupling limit ($\mu 	o \infty$), quasimomentum $\mathbf{K}$ across the entire Brillouin zone, and the statistics (3B, 2+1F, 2+1B).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Feshbach-Schur reduction technique and asymptotic expansions for lattice sums in the small parameter $\delta$.
figures_summary: The notes mention tables summarizing the status of the problem and providing numerical convergence checks for lattice constants and binding energies.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the general framework using Feshbach-Schur reduction, then deriving the explicit effective Hamiltonians for different statistics, followed by determining the zones and critical ratios via matrix criteria, and concluding with proofs of dualities and onset laws.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, exact analytical results for strongly interacting, mass-imbalanced quantum systems, which are highly relevant for modeling quantum simulation experiments using optical lattices.
